correctness.rationale: Exact invariant-normal and Lebesgue-offset disintegration gives expected height-gap divided by expected range; Gaussian radius/direction independence proves this ratio equals the corresponding independent-normal expected spacing ratio. The binomial integral follows from Tonelli; generic crossed simplex edges give k(n-k) vertices and the product face lattice. Gaussian normal tail binomial bounds establish the intermediate order-statistic limit in probability, and an L2-max bound gives uniform integrability, hence the beta logarithmic exponent. Finite script checks 4<=n<=10 combinatorics and normal/Crofton simulation but is not the proof.

value.rationale: Crofton-uniform affine hyperplanes are a canonical geometric sampling model distinct from Haar central sections. Determining a complete combinatorial section-type law in every dimension is natural and mathematically useful; moreover the beta-distributed growth exponent reveals a previously unobvious high-dimensional regime spread across polynomial scales, sharply contrasting the nearly maximal quadratic vertex count of central slices. The value does not rest on small numerical table improvements.
